title: Stack-based Buffer Overflow in TELNET NEW_ENV Option Handling
classified_slop_by: Daniel Stenberg gist 07f7581f6e3d78ef37dfbfc81fd1d1cd (AI slop security reports submitted to curl)
why_rejected: Closed on HackerOne as spam and listed as AI slop in Stenberg's gist. The claimed overflow of the 2048-byte temp buffer in telnet.c suboption() is bogus: the environment data is attacker-/user-supplied via CURLOPT_TELNETOPTIONS (not the remote server), and the quoted length check plus msnprithf's own bound prevent the described out-of-bounds write. No crash is actually demonstrated. The public disclosure JSON exposes no maintainer comment text.
note: report.md reproduces the reporter's large filler 'A' payload strings; exact character counts of the filler may differ slightly from the original submission but the content is otherwise verbatim.
